newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide LPG tracks crude, naphtha, little activity.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide LPG tracks crude, naphtha, little activity.

text.p: Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices moved with crude and naphtha this week, traders and brokers said, with levels little changed by the end of the week after a small increase earlier.

"Maybe buyers and sellers went up during the week, but they then came down again with crude and naphtha," said a Scandinavian trader. "There have been no deals on propane," he added, referring to the large cif propane market in northwest Europe.

He said sellers were still asking prices in the low $190s a tonne cif northwest Europe, but this was deterring buyers. "Petrochemical buyers are looking for naphtha in the mid-$180s, so they would want to pay in the high $170s for propane," he added.
A trader for a large Algerian seller said his company was still looking to move material both to the U.S. and to northwest Europe, but no sales had been made to northern Europe this week.

Another trader said this seller normally moves material in large, 40,000 tonne vessels, but added that only a few petrochemical buyers can take such large vessels, and they are the buyers who are now looking to cheaper feedstocks.
As a result, this seller has been concentrating its sales on the U.S., although it did report moving a 17,000 tonne cargo of butane into Spain at a price related to the Sonatrach official price.
There has been some butane activity on the large cargo market in the North Sea, for the first time in several weeks.

A cargo of 7,000 to 9,000 tonnes was said traded at BPAP +$9 a tonne fob Braefoot Bay in Scotland, giving a fixed price of $168 a tonne fob. Assuming freight of around $14 a tonne, this gives a level on a cif ARA basis of around $182 a tonne, up from the previous sale at $174 a tonne.

On the European coaster market, dealers said, fob levels have remained remarkably stable, at close to $200 a tonne for propane and in the low $160s a tonne for butane, but cif levels have come off sharply.
Propane was talked at around $220 a tonne cif NWE at the beginning of the week, falling to around $205 a tonne by the end. "There are just a lot of ships around," said a trader.
By contrast, a shortage of shipping tonnes is keeping freight levels firm between the Middle East and the Far East.

"It's difficult to get a ship below $30," said a trader. "If it's that tight, it's a sign that sooner or later we'll have a premium over the CP, maybe ahead of the normal time which is August or September."
The tightness is partly because some vessels are being used for floating storage off Japan, he said, and with others being chartered for long haul purposes, "it's enough to give a kind of pressure."

Propane prices are still around Saudi Aramco's benchmark Contract Price (CP) - $5 a tonne fob Gulf, with butane prices close to CP flat fob Gulf. But little spot trade was heard discussed, dealers said.

In the U.S., levels have been broadly stable to slightly weaker, with propane talked at between 34.75 and 35.00 cents a gallon towards the end of the week. Propane is still seen as strong enough to attract material from Algeria.
But a trader noted towards the end of the week that "NYMEX is weaker and our market is pretty comfortable with the overall liquids supply picture."
